evidence: Commented ASEC reconstruction; no main or automatic invocation. No Cargo manifest or deployment context supplied.
Custom rotated 64-byte table, quartet unpacking, prefix length and bitmask decode recover kernel32.dll NUL and GetVolumeInformationW NUL.
run_agent models file reads, XOR 0x27, LZNT1 compression and TCP send to documentation-range 198.51.100.42:8443. No live endpoint is supplied.
Firefox path omits the profile-specific directory; received configuration is decoded then discarded in favor of hardcoded example rules.
Injection helper is uncalled; it writes XOR-transformed bytes and starts at the allocation, not at LoadLibrary. It does not map DLL headers/imports/relocations.
VM screening is real source behavior; retain one suspicious trait.
samples.change: Remove unbound Firefox theft inference; relocate neutral injection, CPUID and vocabulary; add XOR and VM-screening coverage.

evidence: 0x4037cb polls HTTP task responses; 0x4039d6 dispatches commands 1000-1019 from validated response header.
Task 1018 passes response payload at +0x20 to 0x403466. That function binds child stdout/stderr to an inheritable pipe, calls CreateProcessW, reads captured output and packages a response.
0x40558c builds POST and invokes resolved WinInet methods; 0x4056c0 reads response bytes. 0x4059a6 XORs transferred bytes with 0x42.
0x40317d obtains its own image path and passes it to a stack-built cmd /c ping 127.0.0.1 -n 1 &del command through WinExec.
Unsigned VERSIONINFO claims Microsoft Word/WINWORD.exe. No legitimate remote administration provenance supplied. Collector filename is not WannaCry attribution.
samples.change: No sample-specific YAML change; two hostile findings are supported.

evidence: 0x401cb0 dispatches installation mode from configuration DWORD 0x404120, currently 3. Current branch calls Active Setup installer then self-delete.
0x401900 writes HKLM Active Setup StubPath, copies its own image with fread/fwrite, clears/patches the embedded mode tag and launches the copy.
Alternate mode 1 extracts DLL resource 101/type DLL via 0x402460, replaces LanmanServer Parameters/ServiceDLL via 0x401260, and injects via 0x401150.
Injection launches a selected Internet Explorer/notepad/calc process, writes the DLL path into it and starts a remote thread at resolved LoadLibraryA.
0x401390 builds own-image deletion using short path, COMSPEC and /c del, then CreateProcessA.

Resource section is entirely zero, so resource extraction and DLL deployment cannot succeed for the damaged resource. Traits claim surviving code rather than a successful installation. No payload DDoS or ransomware behavior was inferred from banners or collector filename.
